s.t: Next, inside the relay, then the AUX route.
Most of this slice has not been timed. Only the loads, the edit and the score have. Every step also needs its own repository to pass its gate (not drawn).
The relay is transport-zone-relay: a C state machine equal to the router model, on two UDP sockets and a 64 Hz tick. Both ways to route are drawn; the planner tries the model first.
White wires are the sequence the planner runs. Coloured pins are facts a step reads (left) and sets (right).
Part 1. From a moving body to an edited, scored image
A frame that comes too soon is refused and counted, and its bytes are not copied. Checked against the router model's recorded trace (210 ticks); the sockets only on loopback.
A taken frame is copied in, handed out unchanged and sent on as it arrives, so none waits in the relay longer than one tick. A viewer gets six frames a send interval.
transport-zone-relay, in C. Strict C99, no heap, and it never reads a byte of a frame. A zone is four people.
Part 2. Inside the relay: one loop, 64 times a second
one tick for each tick the wall has had
now + 1; a slot silent over 192 ticks is emptied
too long, a 5th person, or a half taken too soon
sendmmsg, from the port of the same half
zr_put: 1 in 5 ticks, burst of two
recvmmsg, up to 32 at a time
The 91 minutes leaves out image-to-mesh and matting: neither has been timed. Dim nodes are the image route, skipped when the dataset mesh is on hand.
The longest chain is: build the simulator, measure which parts lag (60 min), decide soft or rigid, rig. The one GPU is a pin passed from step to step, so GPU steps take turns.
The planner's route for the AUX goal. The planner runs independent steps side by side; the white wire lists them one after another.
